sources.entry: Tox - Distributed, secure messenger with audio and video chat capabilities. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C

summary.one_liner: C reference implementation of Tox, a serverless peer-to-peer encrypted instant messenger library with optional audio/video support.
summary.what_it_does: Provides the toxcore C library for building Tox-based peer-to-peer messaging applications without a central server. It uses libsodium for encryption and authentication. The API is event-driven: applications register callbacks for events such as friend requests and incoming messages, then call tox_iterate in a loop to process network traffic. The README walks through a minimal echo bot that accepts friend requests and replies with each message it receives. The build is CMake-based and, when libvpx and opus are present, also builds an A/V library for audio and video chats. The README also lists static analysis, sanitizer, and fuzzing tools used in the project's testing.
use_cases: build a peer-to-peer encrypted chat application
write a Tox echo or chat bot in C
embed serverless messaging in a C program
add audio and video calls via libvpx and opus
study the Tox protocol reference implementation
how_to_run: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TokTok/c-toxcore (or run git submodule update --init in the repo)
notable: Serverless peer-to-peer design with encryption via libsodium
Callback-based API driven by a tox_iterate main loop
Optional A/V library built when libvpx and opus are installed
Echo bot tutorial in the README walks through the API
Extensive SAST, sanitizer, and fuzzing tooling listed
caveats: README describes the library as experimental and not formally audited; use at your own risk
Security threat model not yet fully specified, per the README
Requires git submodules to be initialized before building
Bots built on it work on a LAN per the README; internet bootstrapping is glossed over in the tutorial
